result:
Understood. I'll write it up once you make one choice: how it gets built. Your answer changes what the design says, so I don't want to pick for you. There are three sensible ways.

1. **Add batch tracking to the taproom app.** New tables go in the same SQLite database on the Pi. Brewers scan sacks with a handheld barcode scanner into a browser page on a tablet in the brewhouse. This is one app and one database file to back up. The cost: a taproom fault could take batch records down with it, and the reverse is also true.
2. **Build a separate small app on the same Pi.** It uses the same tools, but has its own database file. A busy Friday at the bar never touches your traceability records. The cost: a second service to keep running, and a second file to back up.
3. **Buy brewery software** such as Ekos or Breww. These tools already do lot traceability. The cost: a monthly fee, and your records leave the Pi. I don't yet know if they work with your label printer.

**I recommend option 2.** A trace record is only useful if it is complete, possibly years from now during a recall. Keeping that record apart from the tab system protects it. It still reuses everything you already run.

This is a project, not a small change. After you pick, I'll write the full design into `specs/`. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions. One more thing: this folder isn't a git repository yet, so I'll ask before I set one up to commit the spec.

Which way do you want to go?
